reader.requirement: At --std 85 GENERATE takes exactly one operand, either data-name-1 (a 1985 data-name, which SR1 lets be qualified by a report-name and nothing else, so no subscript or reference modifier) or report-name-1, and binds it to detail processing (the named DETAIL group) or summary processing (the report) respectively.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectLevel<2002 adds the 1985 'no more than one detail report group' screen for the report-name form (COBOL ReportGenerateDetailCount, §1985 SR2b); not a format question

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel/Edition in ReportWriterBinder.cs#BindGenerate; grep VisitGenerateStatement/VisitReportGroupReference in Validation/*.cs (none); the grammar rule has no edition predicate
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the format (one operand, data-name optionally qualified by IN/OF report-name, or report-name) is the same shape and the same code at 85 and 2023; only the SR2 detail-count screen is 85-only

reader.notes: The operand is the shared reportGroupReference (cobolWord [IN|OF report-name]); BindGenerate tries the report-name arm only for an unqualified operand and otherwise resolves through ReportGroupResolution, which diagnoses ambiguity. No edition gate touches the format itself.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-004/gen/q04.cob: WORKING-STORAGE 01 DA PIC X. and RD R-1 with 01 DA TYPE DE; GENERATE DA. (unqualified) at --std 85 -> RAN and presented the detail twice (also RAN at --std 2023). q09 adds MOVE "Z" TO DA (also unqualified): RAN; q10 with 02 DA under a WS group: RAN. DA is a nonunique user-defined name explicitly referenced in a Procedure Division statement: cite.py 'OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 (4.3.8.1 Qualification) the text is in the clause; it lies in SR1' for 'No other name has the identical spelling and hyphenation', and 'OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 ... SRL2.1' for 'For each nonunique user-defined name that is explicitly referenced, uniqueness must be established through a sequence of qualifiers which precludes any ambiguity of reference'; SR1 of GENERATE supplies the qualifier (cite.py 'OK §1985:XIII.4.3.3 SR1' for 'Data-name-1 must name a type detail report group and may be qualified by a report-name'), so GENERATE DA OF R-1 is required and GENERATE DA must be refused. ReportGroupResolution.cs#Resolve collects candidates only from report groups (lines 73-79), so a same-spelled non-report data item never makes the reference ambiguous; the reader's note that the resolver 'diagnoses ambiguity' holds only between two RDs. The rest held: q01 GENERATE R-1 with two DE groups -> COBOL6823 (§1985 SR2b, 85 arm); q02 GENERATE R-1 with CONTROL and only a CF body group -> RAN, summary CF lines; q03 no body group -> COBOL2749; q05 DA OF RPT (file-name qualifier) -> COBOL1757; q06 a level-02 entry of the detail -> COBOL1757; q07 plain GENERATE DA -> RAN; q08 GENERATE DB OF R-1 -> RAN with CF at each break.
refuter.corrected: PARTIAL (under-rejects, cause b: the same at every edition, --std 2023 also RAN). Minimal repro: WORKING-STORAGE 01 DA PIC X. REPORT SECTION RD R-1. 01 DA TYPE DE LINE PLUS 1 ... PROCEDURE DIVISION ... GENERATE DA. Expected at --std 85: refused, the unqualified data-name-1 is not unique (§1985:IV.4.3.8.1 rule 1; write DA OF R-1). Observed: compiles and binds to the detail group. The defect is in ReportGroupResolution#Resolve, which the USE BEFORE REPORTING operand and the SUM UPON operand share; it may be homed on the qualification rule's row (§1985:IV.4.3.8.1) rather than this format's. kb/Work: none found (PB365 covers ambiguity between two RDs only).
